takeaways: Big Tech's AI-driven earnings are increasingly fueled by circular capital flows and off-balance-sheet lease commitments, raising concerns about the sustainability of infrastructure spending and underlying enterprise demand.

Global markets are reacting to cooling US inflation and potential rate-hike delays, though rising Japanese bond yields and fiscal fragility in the AI sector pose significant cross-market liquidity risks.

While AI infrastructure demand broadens into networking and defense, regional EV sales remain polarized by policy shifts, highlighting a disconnect between aggressive capital investment and actual consumer adoption.
day_verdict: Major day — market-moving events; read carefully.

items.title: Global markets buoyed by US inflation data, Mideast woes linger
bullets: US Producer Price Index data showed flat month-on-month growth and a 4.7% annual increase, falling short of projections and signaling a potential cooling in inflationary pressures.
The market reaction has pushed Federal Reserve rate hike expectations to December, causing the US Dollar Index to drop below 100 and driving US Treasury yields down by five basis points.
items.reason: Market-moving shift in Fed rate expectations

items.title: Nomura sees resilient H2 CY 26 global economy, but warns of US-Iran tensions, El Niño and AI setback
bullets: Nomura forecasts US core PCE inflation to remain elevated at 3.2% by Q4 2026, suggesting the Federal Reserve may be forced into rapid rate hikes if it continues to hold steady.

The firm identifies significant downside risks to global growth, specifically citing the potential for an AI investment setback, fiscal fragility, and supply-side shocks from El Niño and Middle East hostilities.
items.reason: Strategic outlook on persistent inflation and systemic risks

items.title: Malaysia's central bank upbeat as Q2 growth beats expectations
bullets: Malaysia reported a 6% GDP growth for Q2 2026, outperforming both the 5.8% advance estimate and the 5.4% expansion seen in the first quarter.
Growth is being driven by robust export performance and AI-related infrastructure investments, leading the central bank to revise its 2026 outlook toward the upper end of its 4-5% projection range.
items.reason: Strong regional economic indicator for emerging markets

items.title: Amazon and Alphabet’s Profits Reveal Circular Nature of A.I. Boom
bullets: The current AI investment cycle is increasingly characterized by a circular flow of capital, where massive infrastructure spending by tech giants like Amazon and Alphabet effectively fuels the revenue growth of the very hardware and software providers they rely on.

This dependency creates a feedback loop that may inflate short-term earnings reports, raising questions for investors about the sustainability of capital expenditure levels if end-user demand for AI applications does not materialize at scale.
items.reason: Highlights a critical structural risk in the current AI-driven market rally.

items.title: Alto Ingredients, Inc. ALTO delivered a significantly improved second-quarter 2026 performance
bullets: Despite achieving a significant turnaround with a $16.6 million gross profit and 15 cents EPS, Alto Ingredients shares have plummeted 17% since the earnings release, signaling a disconnect between operational improvements and market sentiment.

The stock's sharp underperformance relative to the broader Consumer Discretionary sector suggests that investors are prioritizing macro-economic headwinds or sector-specific valuation concerns over the company's improved ethanol crush margins and sales volumes.
items.reason: Illustrates a notable earnings-price divergence, providing a case study in market sentiment vs. fundamentals.

items.title: Why ‘Canada is not immune’ to the effects of Japan’s surging bond yields
bullets: Rising Japanese government bond yields are incentivizing domestic investors to repatriate capital, potentially reducing demand for U.S. Treasuries and forcing a higher term premium on long-term debt.
The correlation between U.S. and Canadian bond markets remains high, with approximately 70% to 80% of U.S. yield volatility typically transmitting directly into Canadian benchmark rates.
items.reason: Highlights a structural shift in global capital flows impacting major sovereign bond markets.

items.title: When will mortgage rates go down from close to a one-year high?
bullets: Despite the Federal Reserve's pause in rate cuts throughout 2026, mortgage rates remain elevated near 6.67%, with Fannie Mae projecting these levels to persist through 2027.
The housing market has shown surprising resilience with year-to-date sales up 2.4%, though economists suggest a return to 6% mortgage rates is necessary for a significant market expansion.
items.reason: Provides critical context on the disconnect between Fed policy and consumer borrowing costs.

items.title: China Widening C/A Surplus
bullets: China's current account surplus continues to expand as a result of persistent trade imbalances, driven by high export competitiveness and excess industrial capacity coupled with weak domestic import demand.
Analysts project a slow appreciation of the Yuan to 6.65 USDCNY by end-2026 and 6.50 by end-2027, as authorities balance export competitiveness against potential U.S. tariff pressures.
items.reason: Highlights structural trade imbalances and currency trajectory.

items.title: Asia Economic Calendar: BI Rate, China Data, Japan GDP in Focus
bullets: Upcoming July activity indicators are expected to show continued economic weakness, with retail sales growth projected at a subdued 1.7% and fixed asset investment contracting by 6.3% year-to-date.

Market participants are closely monitoring the 70-city property price index for signs of stabilization in tier-1 and tier-2 cities, while the Loan Prime Rate is expected to remain unchanged at 3.0% and 3.5%.
items.reason: Provides critical forward-looking data points for market sentiment.

items.title: CK Asset Nearly Triples Property Sales to $2.8B as Development Profit Falls 57%
bullets: CK Asset reported a 193% surge in property sales revenue to HK$21.6 billion, driven by luxury project completions, yet development profit contribution plummeted 57% due to compressed margins falling to 3.5%.

The firm recorded significant asset value declines, including a HK$6 billion impairment on its stake in Hui Xian REIT and a HK$1.5 billion drop in investment property values, highlighting ongoing pressure in the commercial real estate sector.
items.reason: Significant earnings report from a major developer indicating margin compression and asset impairment.

items.title: URA posts HK$338 million operating surplus after three years of losses
bullets: The Urban Renewal Authority returned to an operating surplus of HK$338 million in the 2025-26 financial year, ending a three-year streak of losses that had previously forced the body to raise HK$8 billion via bond issuance.

Despite the return to profit, the authority faces ongoing financial challenges in urban redevelopment, necessitating a focus on 'flexible strategies' and the upcoming enhancement of the 'Smart Tender' scheme to support property owners.
items.reason: Signals a potential stabilization in the public-sector urban renewal financing landscape.

items.title: Tech layoffs 2026: Tracking all of the job losses across TikTok, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle, Samsung, Zillow and others
bullets: The technology sector has seen over 175,000 layoffs in 2026, with Oracle leading the trend by cutting 21,000 jobs—approximately 13% of its workforce—explicitly citing AI-driven operational efficiency as a primary driver.

The accelerating pace of workforce reductions, coupled with increased capital expenditure on AI, suggests that major tech firms are prioritizing aggressive cost-cutting to offset the high costs of AI infrastructure deployment.
items.reason: Significant indicator of structural shifts in tech labor and AI-driven cost management.

items.title: How Big Tech’s Earnings Are Inflated by Other Tech Companies
bullets: The current earnings growth in the Big Tech sector is increasingly driven by circular spending, where major cloud providers and software giants are the primary customers for each other's AI-related services.

Investors should be cautious of potential revenue quality issues, as this inter-company spending loop may mask underlying demand weakness from non-tech enterprise customers and inflate top-line growth metrics.
items.reason: Addresses potential systemic risk and valuation concerns regarding the sustainability of AI-driven earnings growth.

items.title: OpenAI talent exodus raises 'huge red flag' ahead of IPO
bullets: The sudden departure of key C-suite executives, including the chief revenue officer and operating chief, creates significant leadership instability as the company prepares for a highly anticipated IPO.
Investors are increasingly wary of the company's $852 billion valuation amid mounting competitive pressure from Google and Anthropic, alongside the proliferation of lower-cost open-weight AI models.
items.reason: Executive turnover at a pre-IPO firm of this scale is a major risk signal.

items.title: Not Micron, Not Sandisk. This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Memory Stock Could Be the Next Nvidia.
bullets: SK Hynix has secured a dominant 58% market share in the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) sector, effectively doubling the combined market presence of its primary competitors, Micron and Samsung.

The company's strategic positioning in the memory supply chain makes it a critical beneficiary of the ongoing AI infrastructure build-out, as demand shifts from raw processing power to specialized memory architectures.
items.reason: Identifies a dominant, under-the-radar player in the critical AI memory supply chain.

items.title: Goldman in talks with investors on Nvidia financing deal after landing prized role, sources say
bullets: Goldman Sachs is actively courting institutional investors to participate in a massive $500 billion financing initiative designed to sustain the AI infrastructure boom.
This complex financial structure aims to provide the necessary capital for continued AI expansion, signaling a shift toward more aggressive, exotic financing models to maintain sector momentum.
items.reason: Significant structural shift in AI capital allocation

items.title: Nvidia, Nancy Pelosi, Cathie Wood Strike Gold With Databricks' $190 Billion Valuation
bullets: Databricks has reached a $190 billion valuation following a new $5 billion funding round, representing a 558.8% appreciation for early investors since the 2023 funding cycle.
Nvidia’s strategic stake in the software giant highlights its broader ecosystem play, as the company continues to diversify its influence beyond hardware into critical AI data infrastructure.
items.reason: Major valuation milestone for a key AI ecosystem partner

items.title: Government could slash EV sales targets as zero emissions mandate comes under review
bullets: The UK government has initiated a formal consultation to potentially reduce the 2030 zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) sales target from 80% to as low as 50%, citing difficult global trading conditions and industry pressure.

While the 2035 deadline for a total phase-out of new petrol and diesel car sales remains unchanged, the proposed flexibility could allow manufacturers to rely more heavily on hybrid vehicles to meet interim compliance obligations.
items.reason: Significant regulatory shift impacting automotive manufacturing strategy and compliance costs.

items.title: Global EV Sales Surge: July Hits 1.85M Units, Up 9%
bullets: Global EV sales reached 1.85 million units in July 2026, a 9% year-on-year increase, though regional performance remains highly polarized with European growth of 33% contrasting against a 27% contraction in North America.

The North American decline is directly attributed to the expiration of federal tax incentives, while European markets are benefiting from robust subsidy frameworks like France's 81% sales surge and Germany's 46% growth.
items.reason: Highlights critical regional divergence in EV adoption driven by government policy changes.

items.title: AI’s infrastructure boom is getting more leveraged — and harder to track
bullets: Hyperscalers have accumulated $1.5 trillion in lease commitments for data centers and equipment, a massive increase from $200 billion five years ago, with $1 trillion currently classified as 'uncommenced' and off-balance-sheet.

The reliance on complex financing structures and derivatives to fund AI infrastructure is creating hidden leverage risks, raising concerns among analysts about future liquidity needs and the ability of AI revenues to justify such capital intensity.
items.reason: Highlights systemic financial risk and massive hidden debt in the AI infrastructure sector.

items.title: Cisco Q4 FY 2026 Earnings Point to Broader AI Infrastructure Demand
bullets: Cisco reported strong Q4 FY 2026 results with $17.25 billion in revenue, exceeding consensus estimates, driven by a 28% year-over-year surge in networking revenue as enterprises and cloud providers upgrade for AI.

The results indicate that AI infrastructure demand is broadening beyond hyperscalers to include public sector, telco, and campus environments, signaling a sustained, multi-sector investment cycle in distributed AI networking.
items.reason: Provides concrete evidence of broad-based, profitable growth in the AI infrastructure supply chain.

items.title: US Space Force gives Rocket Lab $397 million to build threat-tracking 'Flatellites'
bullets: Rocket Lab has secured a $397 million contract from the U.S. Space Force to develop and launch 'Flatellites' for the Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator (SB-AMTI) program, aimed at real-time threat tracking.

This award brings the company's total government-funded defense contract value to $943 million for 2026, highlighting a significant shift toward high-margin national security revenue streams and rapid, responsive launch capabilities.
items.reason: Major contract win significantly bolsters revenue and defense sector positioning.

items.title: Rocket Lab Enters Europe’s Crowded Launch Market
bullets: Rocket Lab is establishing a German subsidiary to provide domestic satellite production and launch services, directly challenging European incumbents like Arianespace and Avio with a superior launch cadence.

With $2.13 billion in cash reserves, Rocket Lab possesses a significant capital advantage over European startups, which are currently competing for a combined €902.2 million in regional government funding, signaling a potential price war.
items.reason: Strategic international expansion threatens regional competitors and signals aggressive market share growth.
